t: Introduction: why a commission examination is needed
n: This session is devoted to the commission examination. In cases of improper performance of professional duties, questions arise in the investigation and in court that require the special knowledge and skills of medicine. In accordance with legislation, in such cases a commission forensic medical examination must be ordered. The session covers the grounds for ordering it, the composition of the commission, the structure of the conclusion, the rights of the participants in the proceedings, and the assessment of the conclusion.

t: Normative basis
n: On the normative basis. The ordering and conduct of a commission examination and the assessment of the conclusion are laid down in the Law "On Forensic Examination", the Code of Criminal Procedure (CCP) and the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). That is, the basis is first of all the Law on Forensic Examination, then the CCP and CPC. In addition, there are special departmental rules for conducting commission forensic medical examinations. Thus the commission examination is an activity regulated jointly by law and departmental rules.

t: Types of examination
n: Types of examination. A primary examination is the initial one. An additional examination is conducted when the conclusion is not sufficiently clear and complete. A repeat examination is ordered if the conclusion is not substantiated or there is doubt about its correctness. A commission examination is conducted by a group of specialists in one field of knowledge, while a complex examination is conducted using different kinds of special knowledge. When a body, a living person or physical evidence cannot be examined directly, an examination on the basis of materials is conducted; it, too, may be primary, repeat, additional or commission.

t: Grounds for ordering
n: The ground for ordering a commission examination is a resolution of the inquiry officer, investigator or prosecutor, or a ruling of the court. The content of the resolution and ruling, stage by stage, is as follows. In the descriptive part the circumstances of the case are briefly set out. Then in the ordering part the type of examination and to whom it is assigned are stated. In the operative part the questions to be resolved by the commission of experts are given. Remember: the commission answers exactly these questions, so it is important that they are formulated correctly.

t: Requirements for the questions
n: There are two requirements for the questions. First, the questions must be precise, clear and consistent with the aims of forensic examination. Second, the questions must not go beyond the competence of the commission of forensic medical experts. That is, the commission is asked to answer only on matters that fall within its authority. Unclear questions, or questions outside its competence, hinder the quality of the examination.

t: Materials submitted to the commission
n: Materials submitted to the commission. The case materials, medical documents and other objects necessary for the examination are submitted to the commission; they are listed in the resolution. In exceptional cases, photocopies signed by the head of the institution and certified with a seal may be used. A commission examination on the basis of separate extracts from the case history and certificates is not permitted. Thus original documents are the main source, a photocopy is only an exception, and an extract or certificate is unsuitable for examination.

t: Additional documents in cases of bringing to liability
n: In cases of bringing to liability, additional documents are also needed. Departmental and other official inquiries conducted earlier must be submitted to the commission. The employee being held liable is given a reference stating his professional training, experience and qualification category. In case of death, the conclusion of the autopsy examination or the pathological record is submitted. The results of additional laboratory tests, that is, histological and forensic chemical results, are also submitted.

t: Missing materials and impossibility of giving a conclusion
n: Missing materials and impossibility of giving a conclusion. Missing case materials may, on the commission's proposal, be requested by the head of the expert institution from the body that ordered the examination. If the question cannot be resolved, if the object is unsuitable or insufficient, or if science does not allow it, the commission draws up a reasoned document on the impossibility of giving a conclusion. Such cases: knowledge is insufficient, the objects are unsuitable or insufficient, science and practice do not allow. As a result a reasoned document is sent.

t: Place of conduct and number of commission members
n: Place of conduct and number of commission members. Commission forensic medical examinations are conducted only in forensic medical examination bureaux; in district, inter-district and city units this is not permitted. The commission consists of not fewer than 3 people, that is, not fewer than three persons. If necessary, in addition to state forensic medical experts, clinical specialists of various profiles may be included. That is, the place is the forensic medical examination bureau, the composition is not fewer than 3 people, and a clinical specialist is added when necessary.

t: Who determines the composition of the commission
n: Who determines the composition of the commission? In the first case, the body that ordered the examination may determine the composition at its own discretion. In the second case, it may include an individual specialist in the commission. The third case: if the composition is not specified in the resolution, the head of the expert institution, in agreement with the ordering body, forms the commission from his own staff. The fourth case: if knowledge is insufficient, the head may give a recommendation on including specialists from another institution.

t: Persons who cannot be members of the commission
n: Persons who cannot be members of the commission. The heads and specialists of the medical institution where the event occurred cannot be included in the commission. Persons who are in any form interested in the outcome of the case also cannot be members of the commission. This restriction ensures the objectivity of the commission. The question of challenging members is considered by the body that ordered the examination, in the manner established by law.

t: Lead expert and rapporteur
n: The lead expert and the rapporteur are special roles in the commission. The lead expert is usually the head of the expert institution or the head of the relevant unit; he organises the work and ensures supervision. The rapporteur on the case draws up the plan of execution, communicates with the person who ordered the examination, prepares the materials for the meeting and familiarises the members with them. The rapporteur also draws up the draft conclusions and supervises the formal preparation of the report. The other members take part in the examination and the conclusion.

t: Equal rights of the members
n: Equal rights of the members. All members of the commission, including the lead expert and the rapporteur, have equal procedural rights and duties. The lead expert's task is to organise the work and ensure supervision, while the rapporteur's task relates to the plan, communication, materials and the draft conclusions. However, this difference in tasks gives no advantage in rights. No one, not even the lead expert, has a privilege or priority in resolving the questions put to the examination.

t: Rights of the commission
n: Rights of the commission. First, the commission has the right, with the permission of the ordering body, to become acquainted with the materials of the criminal or civil case. Second, it may demand that the medical worker being held liable be questioned in the presence of the commission, so that he can give explanations. Thus familiarisation with the case materials takes place with permission, while questioning the employee is a right which the commission may demand.

t: Help from medical institutions and in-patient examination
n: Help from medical institutions and in-patient examination. All medical institutions are obliged to assist the commission in every way. Forms of help: participation of specialists, consultations and laboratory tests. In some cases a person is examined in a hospital on the commission's recommendation and with a referral from the body that ordered the examination. The results of the in-patient examination are submitted to the commission through the ordering body.

t: Examination conclusion: introductory part
n: The introductory part of the examination conclusion. The results are drawn up in an approved form as the experts' conclusion and consist of three parts: introduction, investigation and findings. The introduction states the date, place, basis and the composition of the commission; for the composition, post, academic degree, title, length of service and category are entered. The case, the aim and the questions are also given. The introduction also lists the materials, documents and objects submitted to the commission.

t: Investigation part
n: The investigation part. In this part the essence of the case is briefly set out, with the evidence necessary to resolve the questions. The ground for instituting the case and an extract from the record of inspection of the scene or of the place where the body was found are noted. Then the data from the medical documents are given: the complaint and condition on the day of presentation, dynamic observation, treatment measures, consultations and the consilium, as well as paraclinical results.

t: Investigation part: additional sources
n: Additional sources of the investigation part. For a body, extracts are given from the conclusion of the autopsy examination with its findings, and from the pathological record, that is, the diagnosis and the clinico-anatomical epicrisis. For the laboratory part, additional histological and toxicological data are entered. Extracts from the records of clinico-anatomical and clinical conferences are also given. For the employee and witnesses, extracts are given from the employee's service reference, departmental and non-departmental inquiries, and the records of interrogation of the accused, the victim and the witnesses.

t: Indicating extracts by page of the case file
n: The rule for indicating extracts by page of the case file. All extracts and information taken from documents must be set out with an indication of the page of the case materials on which they are found. In an examination on the basis of materials, extracts are given as quotations, with the exact title of the document, its date and a reference to the serial number of the case. This requirement makes it possible to check every item of information in the conclusion against the case materials.

t: Requirements for the findings
n: Requirements for the findings. The findings contain answers to the questions and must follow from the data of the investigation part of the conclusion and correspond to them. A finding must be objective, scientifically substantiated, sufficiently precise and clear, and not admit different interpretations. Findings based only on subjective, conjectural data, or incomplete, vague or mutually contradictory ones, are not permitted. That is, a finding must be objective, scientifically substantiated, precise and clear, and consistent with the investigation.

t: Declining to resolve questions, and initiative
n: The question of declining to resolve questions, and of initiative. If the objects or the experts' special knowledge are insufficient, the commission must give reasons for declining to resolve certain questions. This applies both where the object is inadequate and where special knowledge is inadequate. On the other hand, on its own initiative the commission may also address in the conclusion circumstances that are important for the case but about which no question was put. That is, if a circumstance about which no question was put is important, it is addressed in the conclusion.

t: Signature and dissenting opinion
n: Signature and dissenting opinion. If a common opinion is reached, the commission draws up and signs the conclusion jointly. If the members' opinions differ, each of them gives a separate conclusion on all or some of the questions. An expert who does not agree with the general conclusion signs only the part with which he agrees, and sets out his dissenting opinion after the general findings and signs it. Thus every member has the right to keep his opinion in written form.

t: Causes, conditions and appendices
n: Causes, conditions and appendices. The conclusion may state the causes of the offence, the conditions that contributed to it, and recommendations for eliminating and preventing it. Illustrative materials are appended to the conclusion and form an integral part of it. Storage rule: the examination materials are kept in the expert institution for the period established by legislation.

t: Sending and disclosure of the conclusion
n: The procedure for sending and disclosing the conclusion. When the examination is finished, the conclusion is sent, together with the case materials and objects, to the body that ordered the examination, that is, to the person. Remember: without the official permission of the ordering body, presenting the conclusion to participants in the proceedings is not permitted. Thus the conclusion goes first to the ordering body, and the participants become acquainted with it only after official permission.

t: Rights of the suspect and the accused
n: The rights of the suspect and the accused are set out in Article 179 of the CCP; this article relates to suspects, accused persons and defendants. Before the examination begins, they may become acquainted with the resolution or ruling. They may challenge the expert and make a recommendation about appointing an expert. They have the right to put additional questions on the questions and materials and to submit additional materials. After the conclusion, there is the right to become acquainted with it and to demand an additional or repeat examination.

t: Medical worker and participants in the proceedings
n: The medical worker and participants in the proceedings. In an examination to assess the medical care provided, the medical worker being held liable has the same rights. Participants attend with the permission of the ordering body, do not interfere in the examination, and may demand explanation of the essence of the methods and results. At the same time there is a limitation: participants in the proceedings cannot be admitted to the stages of the commission's meeting and the drawing up of findings. That is, what is permitted is to ask about the essence of the methods and results, to receive explanations and to attend with permission; what is not permitted is to interfere in the examination, to take part in the commission's meeting, and to be present at the stage of drawing up the findings.

t: Questioning members of the commission
n: Questioning members of the commission. Where there are ambiguities or shortcomings that do not require further examination, members of the commission may be questioned by the inquiry officer, investigator or court. The questioning is conducted only on the existing conclusion. Questioning the members before the conclusion has been submitted is not permitted. That is, the conclusion must come first, and questioning is conducted to clarify ambiguities or shortcomings in that conclusion.

t: Assessment of the conclusion (CCP 187)
n: The assessment of the conclusion is based on Article 187 of the CCP. The commission's conclusion is assessed together with other evidence. Criterion of assessment: the conclusion is checked from the standpoint of scientific substantiation and compliance with procedural norms. For the inquiry officer, investigator and court, the conclusion does not have prevailing force as evidence. If the conclusion is not accepted, this must be reasoned. Remember: the conclusion is important evidence, but it does not stand above other evidence.

t: Two commissions in one case
n: The opinions of two commissions in one case may not coincide. In some cases two or more commission examinations are conducted in one case, and their opinions differ. Then the conclusion of one commission is taken into account, and if the other is rejected, the reasons for rejecting it must be substantiated. Thus, when opinions conflict, the court or the investigation is obliged to justify its choice.

t: Examination on the basis of materials: aim and grounds
n: An examination on the basis of materials is conducted to establish the causes and circumstances of defects in providing medical care. It is ordered when providing the object to the expert is impossible or difficult and when the case contains all the data needed for an answer. As a rule, medical records, certificates, pathological records and conclusions of primary examinations are examined. That is, the aim is to establish the causes of defects, the condition for ordering is the impossibility of providing the object and the sufficiency of data, and the documents examined are those listed above.

t: Instituting the case and the official inquiry
n: Instituting the case and the official inquiry. Cases of medical workers usually arise from a complaint by the patient or relatives, or on the initiative of the administration of the medical institution. Before a criminal case is instituted, a special departmental commission conducts an official inquiry and records the defect, the cause and the causal link in a "Conclusion". Then a criminal case is instituted, and the investigator orders a commission examination. This is the Russian procedure, and it is based on Kharin's data.

t: Objects of examination on the basis of materials
n: Objects of examination on the basis of materials. These are the records of inspection of the scene and of the place where the body was found, and the materials of previous forensic medical examinations. Also the original medical documents in the case file, records of clinico-anatomical conferences and documents of departmental inquiries. The objects also include references on the medical workers being held liable. That is, records, previous examinations, medical documents, inquiry documents and references on employees are taken as objects.

t: Commission, resolution and the expert's competence
n: The commission, the resolution and the expert's competence. The commission for an examination on the basis of materials consists of not fewer than two specialists; one is the lead expert, the other is responsible for organisational support. Each member is obliged to become acquainted personally with the materials submitted. The limit of competence is important: medical questions, the causal link and the establishment of defects belong to the expert commission. The question of intent or negligence, of the employee's guilt or innocence, is not within the competence of the experts; it is within the competence of the court.

t: Questions on defects in medical care
n: Questions to the experts on defects in medical care. On diagnosis: was diagnosis carried out in good time and correctly, and was the clinical diagnosis made correctly? On treatment: was the method of treatment chosen correctly, and was care provided in good time and in full? On intervention: was the medical intervention indicated, how did it affect the patient's condition, was it technically performed correctly, were there complications? And finally: is there a direct causal link between the intervention and the adverse outcome, what defect was allowed, could it have been prevented, was an instruction violated?

t: Professional offences and causes of adverse outcome
n: Professional offences and causes of adverse outcome. A professional offence is an unlawful action or omission in performing a professional duty, in violation of medical science, ethics and deontology, the law and instructions. Adverse outcomes may be associated with a criminal offence, medical error, accident and iatrogenesis. Iatrogenesis is a disease related to the employee's activity. A medical error, however, is a doctor's conscientious mistake in his judgments and actions; it contains no carelessness, inattention, overconfidence or professional ignorance.

t: Types of liability and groups of crimes (Russian legislation)
n: Types of liability and groups of crimes under Russian legislation. A doctor's liability for a professional offence includes criminal, civil-law, disciplinary, administrative and material liability. By social danger, offences are divided into crimes and civil, administrative and disciplinary misconduct. The Criminal Code of Russia lists crimes against the person: death and grave harm through negligence, illegal abortion, failure to render assistance, leaving in danger. Remember: the source sets out the legislation of the Russian Federation; do not confuse it with the articles of the Criminal Code of Uzbekistan.

t: Types of errors and accident
n: Types of errors and accident. In forensic medical practice, the following are distinguished: diagnostic errors, that is, errors in making a diagnosis; treatment errors; organisational errors, that is, errors in organising care; and errors in preparing and drawing up medical documents. An accident is an adverse outcome related to a chance circumstance; a doctor who worked conscientiously could neither foresee nor prevent it. It is not a legal category. Iatrogenesis may also arise as a result of successful treatment of the underlying disease, that is, as a "second disease".

t: Medical care: a contract for paid services (Kharin)
n: Medical care as a contract for paid services, according to Kharin, under the Civil Code of Russia. The Civil Code of Russia includes medical care, including within compulsory and voluntary insurance, among contracts for paid services. The performer, that is, an institution or medical worker, provides the patient with medical care on the instruction of the customer; the customer, as a rule the policyholder, pays for the service. From the general rules: quality and guarantee of the service, provision of information, warning about conditions of use, and liability for improper quality. The quality of the service must correspond to the terms of the contract and to the requirements ordinarily imposed on services of this kind.

t: Conclusion
n: Let us summarise. A commission examination is conducted on the basis of a resolution, in a bureau, by an objective commission of not fewer than three people. The conclusion consists of three parts; the findings must be objective, substantiated and consistent with the data of the investigation. The conclusion does not have prevailing force for the court and the investigation; it is assessed together with other evidence. Remember: the objectivity of the commission, the substantiation of the findings and the assessment of the conclusion together with other evidence are the basic rules of the commission examination.
